description.narrative: IFC expects the Project to (i) contribute to improved food security for consumers through increasing the availability of edible oils and soybean meal to support poultry production in Bangladesh; and (ii) generate economy-wide effects through employment creation and stimulate forward linkages with related sectors. Beyond the Project outcomes, IFC anticipates that the Project will help to reduce food supply volatility in Bangladesh through competitive local production, thereby improving resilience.

The proposed investment is for up to US$40 million (IFC A Loan) to Samuda Food Products Limited (SFPL or the Company) in Bangladesh. The IFC loan will support setting up a greenfield soybean seed crushing plant with a capacity of producing 540 metric tons per day (MTPD) crude degummed soybean oil and 2,370 MTPD of soybean meal (the Project). The Project will improve food safety by boosting the domestic processing of soybeans, supplying crude edible oil for cooking and other edible purposes, and providing soybean meal to local feed producers to support local production of animal protein.
